items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Ernie Powell. Ernie had been in the army with Sy who was a sergent and was director of an army band in which Ernie was a member... The last date I played with Sy, was a small combo gig... The band didn't last very long after that.

ctx.x: The musicians in Carter's band were Joe Thomas, Shad Collins and Russell Smith, trumpetists, and Benny also played trumpet and alto sax. The trombone were Sandy Williams and Milt Robinson. The sax section included Benny, Carl Frye and George Dorsey on altos, Sammy Davis (not Junior) and Stafford (Pazula) Simon, tenors, Sonny White, piano, Ulysses Livington, guitar, Hayes Alvis, bass, Keg Purnell, drums, and Roy Felton, vocalist.

The Coleman Hawkin's orchestra was composed of Joe Guy and Tommy Lindsay, trumpets, Earl Hardy, trombone, Eustice Moore, Jackie Fields, altos, Ernie Powell, tenor, Gene Rodgers, piano, Charles Smith, bass, Arthur Herbert, drums and Thelma Carpenter, vocalist. The only musicians in the band that I had known before going to Europe were Jackie Fields and Gene Rodgers.

Teddy Wilson's orchestra had Adolphus "Doc" Cheatham, Carl(Baura) George and Harold "Shorty" Baker in the trumpet section. Jake Wiley, Floyd "Stumpy" Brady, trombone, Rudy Powell, alto & clarinet, Pete Clark, alto & baritone, George Irish and Bob Carroll, tenor, Al Casey, guitar, Al Hall, bass, J.C. Heard, drums, and Jean Eldridge, Vocals. Buster Harding was arranger and second or stand-in pianist. The only ones in this band that were not new to me were "Doc" Cheatham, "Stumpy", Brady, Rudy Powell, Pete Clark,…
